title: Site Qualification Gates for the Vending Services Program
content:
A workplace site qualifies for a programme of the Vending Services Program where it meets that programme's entry gate on all four counts: the headcount at the site, the monthly sales expected from the estate, whether dedicated power is available for the machines, and whether loading access is available to the site. Each programme's gate stands as printed below.

| Programme | Minimum headcount at the site | Minimum expected monthly sales | Dedicated power required | Loading access required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Single Machine Snack Service | 25 | 320 | yes | no |
| Snack & Cold Beverage Bank | 60 | 850 | yes | no |
| Combination Vending Bank | 140 | 2,100 | yes | yes |
| Fresh Food Vending Service | 220 | 3,600 | yes | yes |
| Campus Vending Network Service | 900 | 11,500 | yes | yes |
| Managed Vending & Kiosk Service | 450 | 7,800 | yes | yes |

Sales figures are monthly and in US dollars. The headcount and sales entries are minima: a site whose headcount stands exactly at the printed figure meets that count, and a site one head below it does not; a site whose expected monthly sales stand exactly at the printed figure meet that count, and a site one dollar below it does not. The power and access entries are requirements rather than figures: where a programme is marked as requiring dedicated power, a site without dedicated power does not meet its gate, and where a programme is marked as requiring loading access, a site without loading access does not meet its gate. Where a programme is not marked as requiring loading access, the availability of loading access makes no difference to that programme's gate.

### Cases either side of a gate (hypothetical sites)

A site of 140 employees with expected monthly sales of 2,100, dedicated power and loading access meets the gate of the Combination Vending Bank on all four counts. The same site with 139 employees does not meet that gate, because the headcount falls below the minimum printed against the programme. A site of 300 employees with expected monthly sales of 4,000 and dedicated power but no loading access does not meet the gate of the Fresh Food Vending Service, whatever its headcount and sales, because loading access is required there; the same site meets the gate of the Snack & Cold Beverage Bank, whose entry does not require loading access.

Note that the gates do not rise uniformly with the size of the programme: the Campus Vending Network Service asks for 900 employees and 11,500 in expected monthly sales, while the Managed Vending & Kiosk Service asks for 450 and 7,800.
